GateFox for macOS

Install the native fox app and manage the gateway using its existing settings.

About 6 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 Build and install locally 02 Updates 03 Development checks 04 Local verification record

The native app sets up and manages gateway connections. It uses the same accounts, model routes, background service, and desktop registration as the command line. The fox appears in its window and Dock icon. The sidebar shows GateFox as its only brand, without a legacy-name subtitle. The window title text is hidden. The sidebar footer shows the version and Submit an issue, which opens the GateFox feedback board in the default browser.

On first launch, the app finds the configuration named by the managed gateway LaunchAgent. If there is none, a fresh installation uses ~/Library/Application Support/GateFox/gateway.json. When only the older ~/Library/Application Support/Subscription Gateway/gateway.json exists, the app keeps that file. Settings lets you choose a different existing JSON file. The app remembers that path locally; it does not copy your provider registrations or change your model choices.

Open Add connection to connect an account, API, or local server and choose its models. An unconfigured Mac opens this wizard automatically. Existing configurations open directly in the dashboard. See setup and connection management for account and model behavior.

Connections identifies whether this Mac hosts its own providers or consumes a shared gateway. Hosts edit their local connections and selected models. Pure shared clients show the serving hostname and a read-only catalog, with retry when the gateway cannot be reached. SSH chats use their remote Mac's gateway; installing the control panel does not copy connections between Macs.

The wizard and connection editors share the same field styling, with matching text and secure-entry insets, a visible focus border, and a minimum height aligned with the action buttons. Manual model fields expand to fit multiple lines.

Select Set up once to enable missing background service and desktop registration. A running service is preserved. Setup refuses a different service configuration or a pending login migration rather than taking over either. Closing or quitting the control panel leaves the gateway running. Its managed service and desktop registration return at login. Closing the last window exits the control panel after its pending setup cleanup. The app offers an optional Full Disk Access invitation after setup. Settings keeps controls for protected-file access, Automation and Local Network available. Access is enabled manually in macOS; see gateway permissions for scope and verification. A signed app can associate the existing startup item with the app's name and fox icon without restarting it. See background identity for signing, staging, and macOS display-refresh behavior.

The overview checks the real loopback health endpoint, the background service, and desktop registration separately, refreshing every thirty seconds while the window is open. Provider rows show configured routes and model counts; they do not claim a working provider login. Use gateway doctor to check those registrations.

Diagnostics shows this Mac's per-model cache use, Copilot session rebuilds, provider failures and reconnect signals over a selected time window. Missing usage is displayed as unreported, and older generic failures stay generic. See diagnostics for coverage and privacy limits.

The wizard opens browser sign-in and reports missing provider prerequisites. Claude and Copilot subscriptions need their official CLIs. The bundled runtime supports API and local-server setup without a separate Node installation.

Build and install locally

Use an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode and a verified extracted gateway release. The app uses only Apple frameworks and adds no dependencies.

npm run build
npm run check
npm test
npm run app:test
npm run app:build -- --backend /absolute/path/to/extracted-gateway-release --install-local
open "$HOME/Applications/GateFox.app"

If --backend is omitted, the builder uses the current installed gateway release under ~/.local/share/gatefox/current, or ~/.local/share/subscription-gateway/current when that is the existing installation. It verifies every payload file against its checksum manifest, rejects symlinks and unlisted payload files, and copies only the release payload. The bundled Node license and all gateway component license files travel with it. Account files and local configuration are outside that payload.

The result is a .app and a ZIP under .state/macos-app/build-*/. The ZIP can be extracted and the app moved to Applications. --install-local installs a new copy in ~/Applications; it refuses an existing app. Quit an earlier copy and move it to Trash before replacing it.

The app prefers the existing managed ~/.local/bin/gateway command. Its bundled release is used for setup when the command is missing. Packaging an app does not upgrade an existing CLI, change its service ownership, or migrate remote hosts. The app build receipt records the app and backend versions separately.

Local builds are not signed for distribution or notarized. Use npm run app:sign with the same Developer ID team on every update. It signs the app, helpers, and an app-owned Node derivative with fixed identifiers and the Automation entitlement. The service then runs installed gateway code through that stable bundled runtime. See Node and tool permissions for initial approvals and verification limits. Before distributing downloads, notarize and staple the complete app and verify Gatekeeper on another Mac. Do not re-sign the Codex desktop app.

Updates

Opening or activating GateFox checks for an app update, throttled to once per five minutes. An available update has a notice on every page and a sidebar indicator. Use Install Update, then Quit & Finish Update when staging is complete. A failed check also appears in the app, with a retry action.

Signed production builds publish through standard GitHub releases. The background updater also checks daily. Activation waits for the GUI to close, preserves the existing gateway service and active work, and retains the prior bundle for rollback. See macOS app updates.

Development checks

npm run app:test runs native configuration/status/process checks and the packaging manifest checks. It uses the installed Xcode developer directory when DEVELOPER_DIR is unset, because Command Line Tools alone omit XCTest. The bundle builder uses the same selection because current SwiftUI state macros also require the Xcode toolchain. Use swift build --package-path native/macos to compile the app without making a bundle.

For real desktop verification, launch the installed app, inspect Overview and Settings, quit, and relaunch. Check that the selected path persists and that the gateway service PID survives closing the app. Exercise setup only against an isolated fixture or an explicitly intended installation. Never stop live chats to verify the control panel.

Local verification record

On October 18, 2026, the Apple Silicon bundle installed and launched locally. The app's actual configuration/status code reported two providers, twenty models, a healthy gateway, an active service, and desktop registration ready. The configuration digest and service PID stayed unchanged after quitting and relaunching the control panel. Fifteen native checks, six packaging checks, and the 1,172-test gateway suite passed.

The desktop was locked during capture. Shotport's app capture and frontmost-window retry both failed with ScreenCaptureKit error -3811, so the rendered Overview, Settings navigation, and Dock appearance still need an unlocked-screen check. The local app and ZIP are not signed or notarized for distribution.

The same verified bundle was also installed over SSH on the MacBook that day. Its existing three providers and twenty-one models reported ready. The rendered Overview, fox logo, Settings page, Refresh shortcut, and quit/relaunch were checked on its unlocked desktop. Its configuration digest and gateway service PID stayed unchanged throughout installation and relaunch.
